title: Siegard project file
description: What a project declares once instead of naming per invocation: `siegard.json`, at the project's own root, holding every root a consumer would otherwise retype at every invocation. It is the consumer's own file — the framework ships this contract and `bin/project.py` to hold the file to it, and writes neither; `/siegard-config` is the one skill that writes it, from what a human tells it. Two resolution rules, and they differ on purpose. `standard` alone may be overridden by an invocation naming a different one, and the report says both existed and which won — a rule's own registry is sometimes worth trying a different one against. `specification_root`, `targets`, `work_root` and `delivery_root` answer only from here: an invocation naming one of these paths instead has no effect, and their absence from this file is a stop, not a question the invocation can answer around it — a structural root is not something worth guessing at twice. Either way, an answer given in a session persists only by this file gaining it.

standard.description: The project's registry of rules, by path relative to this file's own directory — the artifact `schemas/standard.json` is the contract for. `null` is a full answer, not an omission: it declares the project authors no standard, so every entry point takes the honestly narrow path without asking again. That is a different fact from this field being absent, which — like every field's absence here — declares nothing: the project has not gotten to it yet, not decided against it.

specification_root.description: The specification this project's plans implement against, by path relative to this file's own directory. Read exclusively from here (see this schema's own description): a specification root named in an invocation instead of declared here has no effect, so a plan naming one this file does not declare is a plan naming nothing. Its absence here is not a defect to guess around — declaring it is `/siegard-config`'s to do, once.

targets.description: Every target source root this project delivers into, named by the project — `backend`, `frontend`, or whatever it calls them; the framework prescribes none and admits as many as the project holds. Each value is a path relative to this file's own directory. An invocation names a target by its key from here, never by retyping its path, and a key this map does not hold is a target nobody declared.

work_root.description: Where this project's development initiatives live, by path relative to this file's own directory. One initiative is one subdirectory under it, named per invocation as a slug rather than a path — which initiative is a fact of the moment, including a closed one still being reviewed, and the container holding all of them is not. `/plan-work` creates the subdirectory; this file only has to name the container once.

delivery_root.description: Where this project's delivery records live, by path relative to this file's own directory, one subdirectory per initiative — the same slug that names its work root, since one initiative is one plan and one delivery.

slug.description: A name reduced to kebab-case. A name that will not reduce is a refusal, not a transliteration.
